clue.text: A road in a particular location

parts.note: taken as written
a venue is the place where a particular event happens

explanation.surface: Directions telling you a road lies somewhere specific.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle: A, then 'road', then the location; 'in' joins the definition to the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street, so it is a kind of road.

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of shape, so the letters need straightening into a new order

parts.note: all seven letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A grown-up non-professional who is nonetheless clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a non-specialist, someone outside a profession, which is what a layman is.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to insist on and obtain
second meaning: an adjective, precise and rigorous in judgement

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a statement that demand matters; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to insist on payment; as an adjective it means strictly accurate, as a critical eye is.

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the phrase describes a thing having such an appearance

parts.note: 21 across is a word for kinsman, and an uncle is one example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative who looks rather seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to RELATION, and the wordplay wants a particular relation rather than the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means dirty or impure, the state of something that looks unwholesome.

clue.text: A Persian ruler some like in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means reading the preceding words from the end to the start

parts.note: some of something is part of it
like and as both mean in the manner of

explanation.surface: Some people view an old Persian king fondly looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire, a ruler under the king.

parts.note: to aver is to declare or state firmly
south and east are two quarters of the compass; on says they follow in a down clue

explanation.surface: Unwilling to give an opinion about living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters looks like lodgings; in crosswords it is often compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, close in sense to unwilling.

clue.text: Withdrew to write a homily hidden by the tall grass

indicators.note: something kept out of sight by a cover is enclosed by it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
a tract is a short moral or religious treatise, what a homily writer produces

explanation.surface: Someone retired to compose a sermon out of sight in long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The longer piece wraps around the shorter, splitting after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Retracted means drew back or took back, the same as withdrew.

parts.note: pan- is the Greek prefix meaning all, as in pan-American
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Everyone yearning for confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long for' reads as one verb, but 'for' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style, a showy self-assurance.

clue.text: New trend in a mere — a large stretch of water

indicators.note: something new is freshly made, so the letters that follow are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: every letter of the four words
the article after the dash, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion arising on a small lake that becomes a great body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a small lake, which makes the jump to a sea a nice contrast; both a's are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean is the sea between southern Europe and North Africa, a vast expanse of water.

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon a long-winded tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty: it is the last letter of the wordplay and also opens the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse tale of heroes and families.

clue.text: Issue raised by a gold prospector

definitions.text: Issue raised by a gold prospector

parts.note: the surface suggests a matter brought up for discussion; read cryptically, issue is offspring and raised means brought up as a child
the miner, forty-niner of the American folk song, whose darling daughter drowned

explanation.walkthrough: The folk song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' tells of a gold miner in the 1849 rush and his daughter; issue means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Clementine is the miner's daughter in the song, so she is the child a prospector brought up.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to jut out or overhang, as beetling brows do

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense survives mostly in 'beetling cliffs' and 'beetle-browed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a common hard-winged bug and is also a verb meaning to project or overhang.

parts.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
a stance is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: The majority opinion, offered as a sample case.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited as an illustration, the same as an example.

clue.text: The chief taking spirit or port

parts.note: arch- as in archbishop or arch-enemy means chief
an angel is a spiritual being

explanation.surface: A leader hitting the bottle, either spirits or port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'port' both look like drinks; port is in fact the definition, a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a major seaport on the White Sea in northern Russia.

parts.note: the surface suggests a patient who will recover; read cryptically, he is someone who will make others better
seemingly 'of course', but meaning by natural remedies made from plants

explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'he will' as the one who heals rather than the one healed is the whole trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist treats illness with plant remedies, a natural cure rather than drugs.

clue.text: A way the old-fashioned make personal complaint

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
ye is the archaic spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned people's way of lodging a private grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor ailment of one's own body.

clue.text: Class among the Liberals or the Social Democrats

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the following run of words

parts.note: the end of Liberals, all of or, and the start of the
surface padding that completes the political picture and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: A political faction found within the British centre parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberals and the Social Democrats were the two British centre parties that merged in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or category, as a class is.

clue.text: Scatter these about left and right for protection

indicators.note: to scatter is to throw things about at random, so the letters land in a different order
about tells us the jumbled word is spread around the two single letters that follow, joining them in the mix

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An instruction to spread things to both sides as a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place or structure that shields from danger or weather, so it gives protection.

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters before it are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the nine letters of the word, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A sentry going back over his written instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of the Grenadier Guards, one of the British Army's Foot Guards regiments.

clue.text: Set one's heart on way-out coloured girl

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of one
an egress is an exit, a way out

explanation.surface: Fixing one's affections on an unconventional girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set one's heart on' reads as an idiom for desire, but it says to put the middle letter on top of the exit. The answer is a dated term, now offensive, from a 1992 puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old-fashioned term for a Black woman or girl, which the setter rendered with the period's phrase coloured.

clue.text: Implore a certain character to discuss terms

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N, a certain character of the alphabet
to treat with someone is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Begging a particular person to negotiate.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter, and letters' names can be spelt out: EN, EM, ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly, to beg or plead, as to implore is.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: straw or similar material spread for animals to sleep on
second meaning: a set of newborn young, such as kittens or puppies

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about bedding made for tiny pets; 'for' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the straw spread in a stall and a brood of young born at one time.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the act of narrating
second meaning: a link between things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' reads as an adjective (significant) but is the noun for recounting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an account or narration and a link or association between two things.

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that army ants are huge beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier ants are a real caste of ant, so the first two words look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Giants are beings of huge size in myth and folklore.

clue.text: Saying take little notice with advancing years

parts.note: an ad is a small advertisement, a notice in a paper
age is what advancing years bring

explanation.surface: Advice to pay less attention as one gets older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take little notice' reads as ignore, but little notice is a small advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional proverb, a saying handed down.

clue.text: The band will accept drinks — there's a revelation!

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a stripe is a band of colour
cups of tea are drinks

explanation.surface: Musicians agreeing to accept a round of drinks, to general surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' wants to be musicians; it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease reveals the performer's body bit by bit, a literal revelation, said with a wink.

parts.note: taken as written
a stake is money laid as a bet

explanation.surface: A post driven in to hold something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'support' broken in two; read it as one word. 'Stake' looks like a wooden post but is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing, which is to support them.

parts.note: re means regarding or about
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Continuing to worry about an injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb (yet) but is the noun for distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a glass vessel with a long bent neck used for distilling, a kind of laboratory still.

clue.text: Look for the small change in a party

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the coin inside the following group word

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
p is a penny, the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: Searching for loose coins at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for' reads as one verb meaning search, but 'Look' alone is the definition and 'party' is a faction, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect means appearance or the way something looks, so it is a noun synonym of look.
